title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether Contracts Signed by an Enterprise That Has Been Lawfully Declared Bankrupt by a People's Court, with the Permission of the Court to Engage in Business Activities Prior to the Conclusion of the Bankruptcy Proceedings, Are Valid

articles.content_en:
Fa Shi [2000] No. 43

Sichuan Higher People's Court:

Your court's Chuan Gao Fa [1999] No. 23, "Request for Instructions on Whether Economic Contracts Signed with Permission of the People's Court for Business Activities after the Enterprise Has Been Declared Bankrupt According to Law but Before the Conclusion of Bankruptcy Proceedings Are Valid," has been received. Upon research, we reply as follows:

After an enterprise has been declared bankrupt by the People's Court, the bankrupt enterprise shall cease its production and business operations from the date of the People's Court's ruling declaring bankruptcy. However, with the permission of the liquidation group, the bankrupt enterprise may, prior to the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, engage in production and business operations related to the liquidation work in the name of the liquidation group. The liquidation group shall report the circumstances of engaging in such business activities to the People's Court. If a contract entered into by the bankrupt enterprise during this period is not in the name of the liquidation group and is not related to the liquidation work, it shall be deemed invalid.

If there is any inconsistency between the judicial interpretations previously issued by our court and this Reply, this Reply shall prevail.

This is the reply.
